ut_bridal_veil_falls_area.blurb: Bridal Veil Falls is a winter ice and mixed venue in Provo Canyon, in the southern Wasatch, and ranks among the busiest ice spots in the canyon. The frozen falls share the cliff with older bolted mixed lines, and more ice and mixed climbing sits on the higher rock tiers. There are seventeen climbs: about ten mixed, running from M5 to around M10, and seven ice, from WI3 to WI6 with most at WI5. It is a short walk from where you leave the car, so it works for a quick day, but on weekends with good ice you should expect other parties on the lines.

ut_reptilian_wall.blurb: Reptilian Wall is a sunny sandstone crag in Long Canyon, reached from Potash Road near Moab, and a good choice for cooler months. It is split into a left wall and a right wall with a short hike between them, and most of the lines are on the right side. All 17 climbs are trad crack and corner lines in the 5.10 range, with about four at 5.11 and two at 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on desert cracks. Long Canyon as a whole is a quieter alternative to Indian Creek. Wet sandstone is fragile, so wait after rain.

ut_s_curve_upper_wall.blurb: The Upper Wall is the higher of the S-Curve cliffs beside the road in Big Cottonwood Canyon, reached by following a gully above the east end of the Lower Wall. It is steep, bolt-protected sport climbing, with 13 sport lines and four trad routes. Grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11, with a few 5.8 and 5.9 lines and two easy trad climbs around 5.5 and 5.6. Compared with the Lower Wall, this cliff is more broken and not as large. Most routes lower off with a single rope, but a few finish with a walk-off to the west.

ut_solstice_the.blurb: The Solstice is a south-facing limestone sport crag in the Utah Hills west of St. George, and the third and most separate of the Woodbury Road crags. It is a fine winter wall for moderate climbers: 17 bolted routes, mostly 5.9 and 5.10, with two at 5.11 plus a single 5.6 and 5.7. The face starts low-angled and steepens gently, with a mild bulge in the middle where the harder lines go. The limestone is textured, with chert knobs and small pockets, and feels sharp and slippery low down, but the bolts are close together.
ut_solstice_the.parking_note: The dirt road in is rough and steep in places: a high-clearance vehicle can reach the end, while an ordinary car should stop early and walk the loose, steep stretch.

ut_moon_lake.blurb: Moon Lake is a small, high-elevation climbing spot at roughly 8,700 feet in the Vernal area of northeast Utah, with a view over the lake. A short list of seven trad lines runs from 5.7 up to 5.11, and a scatter of boulder problems sits along the trail below, mostly V1 and V2 with a few much harder ones up to V7. Expect a real walk to reach the cliff, which sits high above the trail on the west side of the lake. The wider Vernal area is remote and rock quality varies, so check holds and anchors before trusting them.

ut_fat_albert_boulder.blurb: Fat Albert Boulder is one of the larger blocks in the Cabbage Patch, a bouldering zone on the north side of the road in Little Cottonwood Canyon, and it holds the most problems of any boulder there. Seventeen problems cover a broad spread: mostly V1 to V4, with a couple at V5 and V6 and one at the top end near V8, plus one very easy line. Several of the best-known lines are on or beside the arete. Landings can be awkward on some problems, so bring two pads and a spotter.

ut_cone_area_the.blurb: The Cone is a small cone-shaped formation of welded tuff beside Highway 56, about 12 miles west of Cedar City, and an easy place to introduce beginners or kids to roped climbing. The sport routes and one top rope run from 5.7 to 5.9, and a dozen boulder problems are scattered nearby, from VB to V5 plus one hard V8. The rock is sharp and grainy, which suits smearing. Some shade is available, and the walk from the car is tiny, though traffic noise from the road can make it harder to talk to your partner.
ut_cone_area_the.approach: A very short walk on a well-worn trail from the pullout.
